answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, slowly earned stake rather than the number of agent identities. For example, agents post a bond that can be slashed when an auditable task is proven fraudulent; reputation and voting weight accrue only after completed work survives review. One operator can still create a river of fake agents, but each must lock capital and build a distinct track record, making a coordinated voyage costly and risky. A trusted kernel can enforce the same rules consistently.
